summary: EPIC-004 is decomposed into five dependency-ordered tickets covering deterministic integrity generation, live validation, accepted evidence, retries and recovery, and aligned fixtures and guidance.

tickets.title: Generate canonical integrity metadata from artifact bytes
tickets.description: Provide deterministic, atomic generation of checksum-derived handoff evidence from selected artifact bytes so agents never author digest values.
acceptance_criteria: Repository tooling populates or updates checksum-derived fields from real artifact bytes without caller-supplied digests.
Identical ordered inputs and bytes produce byte-identical canonical output, while a one-byte change produces a deterministic checksum change or mismatch.
Unavailable, ambiguous, or failed generation leaves prior evidence unchanged and reports an actionable recovery step without a manual fallback.
Automated tests prove repeatability, canonical output, one-byte sensitivity, and failure atomicity.

tickets.title: Enforce live artifact integrity and safe paths
tickets.description: Verify exact artifact bytes and resolved repository containment during standalone validation and again immediately before ingest persistence.
acceptance_criteria: A handoff passes only when every artifact is an allowed readable regular file inside the repository and its computed SHA-256 matches exactly.
Missing, unreadable, directory, duplicate, self-referential, repository-escaping, and symlink-escaping paths fail with artifact-specific reasons.
Ingest repeats integrity verification immediately before persistence and rejects evidence changed after standalone validation.
Every integrity failure leaves workflow status and epic lifecycle unchanged and reports deterministic recovery guidance.
Automated tests cover the happy path, one-byte and line-ending changes, all unsafe path classes, stale validation, and unchanged-state guarantees.

tickets.title: Preserve tamper-evident accepted evidence
tickets.description: Persist the accepted handoff and exact verified artifact versions so later validation and resume can detect tampering without relying on mutable live files.
acceptance_criteria: Successful ingest durably preserves integrity evidence for the handoff and exact artifact bytes verified before transition.
Full harness validation and sprint resume identify modified, replaced, missing, or corrupt accepted evidence.
A later approved role can change a live product file while the earlier accepted version remains valid and inspectable.
Partial or failed persistence never becomes accepted and leaves the last trustworthy checkpoint and epic lifecycle unchanged.
Automated tests cover canonical preservation, tampering, replacement, absence, later live-file changes, and interrupted persistence.

tickets.title: Preserve distinct retry evidence and deterministic recovery
tickets.description: Give every retry distinct immutable evidence and make interrupted evidence handling safely and deterministically resumable.
acceptance_criteria: Every retry has evidence identity distinct from prior attempts for the same role, round, and ticket.
Reuse or overwrite of prior accepted evidence is rejected before workflow or epic state changes.
All earlier failed and successful attempts remain inspectable and integrity-verifiable after subsequent retries.
Interruption at any durable boundary resumes without accepting partial evidence, duplicating an accepted transition, or losing the trustworthy checkpoint.
Automated tests cover retries, collisions, overwrite attempts, retained history, repeated recovery, and boundary interruptions.

tickets.title: Align fixtures and operating guidance with the integrity boundary
tickets.description: Make examples, end-to-end regressions, and operating documentation accurately reflect live integrity and recovery behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each example uses verified deterministic fixtures or an explicit schema-only mode that cannot be accepted as live ingest evidence.
Documentation explains the trust boundary, byte comparison, canonical preservation, attempt identity, tamper failures, and recovery actions.
Documentation does not treat visual comparison, agent-authored hashes, approval, merge, or deployment as integrity proof.
End-to-end tests cover every epic integrity and recovery boundary while existing workflow, gate, resume, validation, lint, and production-build checks pass.

risks: Self-referential handoff integrity can create an impossible checksum cycle unless the evidence boundary is explicit.
A validation-to-ingest race can accept changed bytes unless verification is repeated at the durable transition.
Preserving accepted versions must not make legitimate later edits to live product files appear as historical tampering.
String-based containment or symlink traversal can admit evidence outside the repository trust boundary.
Retry identity collisions or partial writes can erase evidence or cause an interrupted attempt to appear accepted.
Existing placeholder examples may be mistaken for ingestible evidence unless their validation mode is unmistakable.

approval_request.question: Approve the five-ticket dependency-ordered plan for EPIC-004?
